subtitle: How Udayaditya Raised Stone and Song to Save a Broken Kingdom

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a partly ruined hill-fort and a rising temple in twilight
panels.action: Udayaditya stands on the rocky hill of Udaipur in present-day Madhya Pradesh, cloak stirred by evening wind, watching temple masons lifting carved stone blocks over the scarred ruins of an older age.

dialogue.text: In broken Malwa, after Bhoja’s fall, Udayaditya forged a different weapon of power—stone, verse and memory.

i18n.hi: टूटी माळवा में, भोज के बाद, उदयादित्य ने नई ताकत गढ़ी—पत्थर, कविता और स्मृति की।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view over central India, gently pushing in toward Malwa plateau
panels.action: A vast map-like vista of the Malwa plateau shows faded outlines of Bhoja’s old realm, Dhara at the center, with neighboring Solanki and Kalachuri domains pressing in from west and east.

dialogue.text: Around 1055 CE, Bhoja died and Malwa fractured. Solanki kings from the west and Kalachuris from the east moved into the gap.

i18n.hi: लगभग १०५५ ई., भोज मरे और माळवा बिखर गया। पश्चिम से चालुक्य, पूरब से कलचुरी उस खाली जगह में घुस आए।

panels.shot: somber interior wide of a plundered court hall
panels.action: A deserted audience hall in Dhara lies half-ruined; broken pillars and toppled statues hint at sack and flight, with dust motes in dim light and abandoned ceremonial umbrellas on the floor.

dialogue.text: Bhoja’s capital, Dhara, lost its certainty. Later chroniclers remembered confusion: rival claimants, raids, and kings whose dates blur in the dark.

i18n.hi: भोज की राजधानी धारा डगमगाने लगी। बाद के लेखक बस अराजकता याद रखते हैं: दावेदार, हमले, धुंधले पड़ते राजा।

panels.shot: medium shot, side profile of Udayaditya in a small, makeshift camp court
panels.action: A younger Udayaditya sits on a plain wooden seat in a temporary camp, maps spread before him and only a handful of officers around, his face lined with worry yet stubborn resolve.

dialogue.text: Out of this haze emerges Udayaditya—described in later prashastis as Bhoja’s brother, not his rival, yet ruling a diminished, threatened Malwa.

i18n.hi: इसी धुंध से उदयादित्य उभरते हैं—बाद की प्रशस्तियों में भोज के भाई, नहीं प्रतिद्वन्द्वी, पर शासन एक सिकुड़ी, डरी हुई माळवा पर।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Udayaditya’s eyes over a flickering oil lamp
panels.action: Udayaditya leans over a rough parchment in lamplight, shadows deepening the lines at his brow as he studies reports of lost forts and shifting allies.

dialogue.speaker: udayaditya
dialogue.text: Steel can reclaim towns. But who will believe we still deserve this throne?

i18n.hi: लोहे से शहर वापस लिए जा सकते हैं। पर कौन मानेगा कि यह सिंहासन अभी हमारा है?

panels.shot: medium shot of Udayaditya in counsel with a learned Brahmin at a camp shrine
panels.action: Under a modest canopy beside a village shrine, Udayaditya consults an elderly Brahmin scribe who holds a stylus and palm leaf, while a small idol and incense stand behind them.

dialogue.text: The sources are silent on his early battles, but clear on his choice: to rule by rebuilding legitimacy, not only by the sword.

i18n.hi: शुरुआती लड़ाइयों पर स्रोत चुप हैं, पर एक बात साफ है: वे ताज की वैधता फिर से गढ़कर राज करना चाहते हैं, सिर्फ तलवार से नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of the rugged hill-country of Udaipur, Madhya Pradesh, at dawn
panels.action: Atop the rocky hill of Udaipur in Madhya Pradesh, sparse scrub and an old fort outline frame Udayaditya as he surveys the surrounding countryside, pointing toward a bare plateau where the future temple will rise.

dialogue.text: Sometime before 1105, he chose a rocky height at Udaipur—not the later Rajput city in Rajasthan, but a hill in Malwa—to make his answer in stone.

i18n.hi: ११०५ से पहले, उसने माळवा के उदयपुर की चोटी चुनी—राजस्थान वाला नहीं, यहाँ का—अपना जवाब पत्थर में लिखने के लिए।

panels.shot: dynamic construction wide, low-angle, with scaffolding and workers
panels.action: Masons, carpenters and laborers swarm around the rising Neelkantheshvara temple; stone blocks are hoisted by ropes, while Udayaditya stands among them, cloak tucked, speaking quietly with a chief architect.

dialogue.text: Here the Neelkantheshvara temple took shape, a late-eleventh-century Paramara monument, its style still echoing Bhoja’s age but built under Udayaditya’s fragile rule.

i18n.hi: यहीं नीलकण्ठेश्वर मंदिर उठा—ग्यारहवीं सदी का परमार धरोहर, शैली भोज के युग की, पर नींव उदयादित्य के डगमगाते राज की।

panels.shot: close-up on a carved stone lintel being set in place
panels.action: Artisans carefully slide an intricately carved lintel into position, sculpted with deities and floral patterns; in the background Udayaditya watches, hand resting on the hilt of his sheathed sword.

dialogue.text: Every beam and bracket proclaimed survival. In an era of rival powers, a great temple said: the Paramaras still build, still endow, still protect Shiva’s abode.

i18n.hi: हर शिला, हर पट्टिका ने कहा: हम जिंदा हैं। दुश्मनों के दौर में, विराट मंदिर बोल उठा—परमार अब भी रचते हैं, दान देते हैं, शिव की रक्षा करते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot inside the nearly finished temple hall
panels.action: Inside the cool stone hall, shafts of light fall on freshly carved pillars; Udayaditya walks barefoot with folded hands, priests and craftsmen behind him, gazing up at the high sanctum doorway.

dialogue.text: The Neelkantheshvara temple was more than devotion. It was a visible claim that the Paramara house still patronised gods, scholars and villages across a recovering Malwa.

i18n.hi: नीलकण्ठेश्वर महज़ भक्ति नहीं था। यह दावा था कि परमार वंश अब भी देवता, विद्वान और गाँवों के रखवाले हैं, उठती हुई माळवा भर में।

panels.shot: close-up of a stone slab being smoothed for inscription
panels.action: A polished vertical stone slab stands ready, its surface smooth; a craftsman kneels with chisel raised, while Udayaditya, thoughtful, gestures as if dictating to an unseen poet beside him.

dialogue.text: Alongside the temple, he turned to another tool of kingship: the prashasti, the courtly eulogy carved in stone.

i18n.hi: मंदिर के साथ उसने राज की दूसरी औज़ार पकड़ी: प्रशस्ति—दरबारी स्तुति, पत्थर पर खुदी हुई।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on inscribed Nagari letters being etched
panels.action: The chisel bites into stone, forming crisp Nagari letters line by line; tiny stone flakes fall as the beginning of a long Sanskrit verse appears on the slab.

dialogue.text: The Udaipur Prashasti, composed around 1105 CE, would fix his lineage, praise his virtues, and reach back to Bhoja to stitch a fractured past into a coherent story.

i18n.hi: उदयपुर प्रशस्ति, लगभग ११०५ ई. की, उसकी वंशावली ठोंक देगी, गुण गाएगी, और भोज तक लौटकर बिखरे अतीत को एक कहानी में सिल देगी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Udayaditya listening to a court poet recite in the temple courtyard
panels.action: In the temple courtyard, a court poet stands with palm leaf in hand, reciting with uplifted arm, while Udayaditya sits on a low throne, attendants around, listening with controlled pride.

dialogue.text: We do not hear every word now, but the inscription’s voice survives: Udayaditya as protector, as Bhoja’s kin, as restorer of dharma in Malwa’s shaken heart.

i18n.hi: सब पंक्तियाँ अब नहीं सुनाई देतीं, पर शिलालेख की आवाज बची है: उदयादित्य बतौर रक्षक, भोज का रक्त, डगमगाती माळवा में धर्म का पुनर्स्थापक।

panels.shot: documentary cutaway, scholar’s-eye view of inscription and modern book
panels.action: A split composition shows, on one side, the weathered Udaipur inscription slab in situ; on the other, a modern scholar’s desk with H.V. Trivedi’s CII volume open, transcription and translation neatly laid out.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, H.V. Trivedi and others would carefully read these lines, using them to reconstruct Udayaditya’s place in a confused succession.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, एच. वी. त्रिवेदी व अन्य ने इन पंक्तियों को पढ़–पढ़कर, उलझी उत्तराधिकार कहानी में उदयादित्य की जगह तय की।

panels.shot: wide shot of an imagined battle tableau in distant background, contrasted with calm temple in foreground
panels.action: Far in the hazy distance, silhouettes of soldiers and banners hint at skirmishes, while in the sharp foreground the Neelkantheshvara temple stands still, its shikhara rising calm against the sky.

dialogue.text: The Nagpur Prashasti would later boast of his son Lakshmadeva’s sweeping conquests, but scholars warn of panegyric exaggeration in these claims.

i18n.hi: नागपुर प्रशस्ति बाद में उसके पुत्र लक्ष्मदेव की विजयों का ढोल पीटेगी, पर विद्वान चेताते हैं: यह शाही बढ़–चढ़कर कही हुई बातें भी हो सकती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of a scholar figure gesturing between lineage chart and question mark
panels.action: A modern historian in a study stands beside a wall chart of Paramara names with dotted lines and question marks, indicating uncertainties around figures like Jayasimha I and the exact sequence after Bhoja.

dialogue.text: K.N. Seth, Pratipal Bhatia and Arvind K. Singh all note gaps: Jayasimha’s identity, dates, and some campaigns remain uncertain beneath the polished praise.

i18n.hi: के. एन. सेठ, प्रतिपाल भाटिया और अरविन्द के. सिंह सब खाली जगहें दिखाते हैं: जयसिंह कौन, कब, किन लड़ाइयों में—सब कुछ प्रशंसा की चमक के नीचे धुंधला।

panels.shot: low-angle interior shot of Udayaditya in the sanctum doorway, silhouetted
panels.action: Udayaditya stands at the threshold of the Neelkantheshvara sanctum, folded hands raised toward the unseen linga inside, his figure framed by carved door jambs and the faint glow of lamps.

dialogue.speaker: udayaditya
dialogue.text: Let this stone outlast battles. Let it tell who we were.

i18n.hi: ये पत्थर जंगों से लंबा जिएं। ये कहें, हम कौन थे।

panels.shot: present-day wide shot of the surviving Neelkantheshvara temple, slightly weathered
panels.action: In present-day light, the Neelkantheshvara temple at Udaipur stands weathered but proud, with worn carvings, a few pilgrims ascending the steps, and trees growing around the old hilltop site.

dialogue.text: Today, the temple and its inscription remain, quiet witnesses to a king who rebuilt power through patronage, memory and carefully carved words.

i18n.hi: आज भी मंदिर और उसका लेख खड़े हैं, खामोश गवाह एक राजा के, जिसने सत्ता को दान, स्मृति और नुकीले शब्दों से फिर से गढ़ा।

panels.shot: final contemplative aerial pull-back from temple to the wider Malwa landscape
panels.action: The view rises above the Neelkantheshvara temple, revealing the broader Malwa landscape of fields, villages and distant towns stretching to the horizon under a soft sky.

dialogue.text: In Udayaditya’s Malwa, recovery meant more than winning back land; it meant inscribing a story that defeat could not erase, in stone that still speaks across nine hundred years.

i18n.hi: उदयादित्य की माळवा में पुनर्जागरण सिर्फ ज़मीन जीतना नहीं था; यह कहानी पत्थर में दर्ज करना था, जिसे हार भी नहीं मिटा सके—ऐसी शिला में, जो नौ सौ बरस बाद भी बोलती है।

title_i18n.hi: युगों तक टिकने वाली उदयादित्य की रचना

subtitle_i18n.en: How Udayaditya Raised Stone and Song to Save a Broken Kingdom
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे उदयादित्य ने पत्थर और गीत से टूटा राज्य बचाया
